name: reviewer
content: Approve. The normalization keeps the existing guards: an empty string still fails the `any(match.groups())` check and a leading `-` still fails `fullmatch`, so `test_rejects_empty` and `test_rejects_negative` keep passing. The error message still shows the caller's original text, which is what we want. Optional follow-up: `format_duration` does not emit days, so `format_duration(parse_duration("1d"))` returns "24h".
reasoning_content: The diff changes two things: the unit table gains d=86400 and the regex gains an optional days group before hours. Input is normalized with ''.join(text.split()).lower(). Edge cases: '' -> normalized '' -> fullmatch succeeds with all groups None -> any() is False -> ValueError, good. '-1h' -> '-' is not matched -> ValueError, good. '1H 30M' -> '1h30m' -> 5400. Round trip: format_duration has no days branch, so 86400 -> '24h'. Not covered by the failing tests; mention it, don't block.

content:
Fixed. The cause was `_PATTERN` in src/timeparse/duration.py: it matched only compact lowercase input and had no day unit, so "1h 30m", "2H15M" and "1d2h" raised ValueError.

Changes (src/timeparse/duration.py only, tests untouched):
- `parse_duration` strips all whitespace and lowercases the input before matching.
- Added `d` (86400 s) to `_UNITS` and to `_PATTERN`.

All 14 tests in tests/test_duration.py pass. The reviewer noted that `format_duration` still has no days branch; I left that for a separate change.
